value.rules_markdown:
- One responsibility per module, core types in module-local `types.rs`, one port trait per file in `src/ports/`.
- Declare every CLI subcommand even if its milestone has not landed.
- `src/server/` is the only production surface; never run as a GitHub Action or distributed.
- Presets are data, not code; add a preset as a new folder, never a new module.
- Never edit the `vendor/tinyagents` submodule; change it upstream and bump the pin.
- One document per `src/` module at `docs/modules/<module>/README.md`.
- Declare credential-needing examples in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` to prevent CI builds.
- Default build is offline; gate any network access behind a feature (`harness`, `github`, `serve`).
- Use rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` for modules/files, `PascalCase` for types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Open every file with a `//!` module doc describing its role and feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; state why a flag or ordering is load-bearing.
- Public items carry doc comments; use `///` on Clap fields to generate help text.
- Tests live in-crate: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, moving to sibling `test.rs` when large. No `tests/` dir.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; `MockForge` records what would have been written.
- Cover lane behaviour with golden tests asserting findings surviving filtering, dedupe, and capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split long topics into focused files.
- The model never holds a write token; mint write credentials only in `src/apply/` after model calls.
- Never execute contributor code; read the diff and tree, do not build or run target repo scripts.
- Treat PR bodies, comments, and diffs as untrusted input; fence and label them as data in prompts.
- Model verdicts are advisory; only deterministic policy in `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` mutates GitHub.
- Report found secrets by type and location only; never put the value in comments, summaries, or logs.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; keep commits small and commit each validated slice.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
